title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
The artificial intelligence industry faces significant upheaval following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation amid allegations of espionage and congressional scrutiny over past China sales. This has triggered an investigation by Democrats and raised concerns about Nvidia's open-source commitments, particularly the Hugging Face acquisition. Simultaneously, Nebius is expanding its neocloud infrastructure with a $40 billion investment, while SoftBank reports substantial losses on AI turbine preorders.

Market analysts are reassessing hardware investments due to Huang’s departure, and venture capital is focusing on deep tech applications following recent data breaches at AI infrastructure providers like Fireworks AI. Globally, Microsoft services are experiencing widespread outages impacting productivity tools, though the cause remains unclear. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy welcomed US involvement in peace talks with Russia, and Ukrainian drone strikes successfully targeted a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea. The FBI issued warnings about sophisticated North Korean hacking campaigns utilizing deepfake video calls.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
A significant global repricing event unfolded overnight, marked by a surge in US Treasury yields, a liquidation of safe-haven gold, and divergent performance across Asian equities. US equities experienced a robust risk-on rally, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 rising sharply, however, underlying market stress was evident due to the 5.10% spike in the 10-year Treasury yield. This triggered a rally in the US Dollar Index and increased WTI crude prices. Gold suffered a dramatic five percent decline as higher real yields eroded its appeal.

Asian markets presented a stark contrast: Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 surged, driven by semiconductor strength, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng and Shanghai Composite indices declined due to property sector concerns and economic anxieties. European bourses reacted negatively to high inflation prints from key nations. US equity futures are currently positive, anticipating continued gains for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100, though institutional desks are managing risk amid expanding term premiums. Key catalysts today include digesting global inflation data, monitoring the sustained rise in yields, and adjusting positions ahead of the weekend. The market remains sensitive to headline-driven movements given elevated yield pressures and a sharp decline in gold prices.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
Here’s a summary of the AGI Era Post-Market Recap for November 13, 2026:

The market experienced a significant rally Friday, with the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, and Dow Jones all posting substantial gains. The S&P surged 2.51%, the Nasdaq jumped 3.53%, and the Dow climbed 2.07%. This positive movement occurred despite earlier concerns about rising Treasury yields and a strengthening dollar.

However, volume was surprisingly low across the major indices, particularly in tech, suggesting limited institutional buying support. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) decreased, indicating reduced market fear. Despite this, the 10-Year Treasury Yield rose sharply to 5.15%, and the Dollar Index also climbed, presenting potential headwinds for equities.

Energy stocks (XLE) led the gains due to higher crude oil prices, while financials (XLF) and utilities (XLU) also performed well, reflecting a risk-on sentiment. Notably, technology (XLK) bucked the trend, driven by strong performance from Tesla, which soared nearly 9%.

Despite Nvidia’s significant drop – over 12% – and Microsoft's modest decline, the broader “Magnificent Seven” tech companies showed resilience. Traders are closely watching the continued hawkish stance of the Federal Reserve and its impact on Treasury yields and the dollar, considering them key risks for equities moving forward.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The escalating Nvidia fallout has exposed critical weaknesses in Western export controls, triggering a geopolitical crisis. Singapore is under scrutiny due to its role in facilitating the illicit transfer of advanced silicon to China, while German intelligence agencies have gained expanded counter-sabotage powers amid concerns about drone reconnaissance targeting European infrastructure.

Simultaneously, Moscow continues its covert operations, including a recent assassination attempt linked to a Ukrainian figure, highlighting the ongoing “shadow war” despite diplomatic efforts. 

Within the U.S., Treasury Secretary Scott Besant publicly accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department of failing to enforce semiconductor restrictions, revealing systemic bureaucratic infighting and compliance vacuums. This leakage allows strategic rivals like China to circumvent sanctions by utilizing compliant intermediaries. 

Analysts predict a surge in scrutiny of third-party logistics firms in Singapore and potential shifts in tech shipping insurance premiums through the Malacca Strait as indicators of this regulatory fracture. The situation underscores the vulnerability of the global semiconductor supply chain and the effectiveness of unilateral technological sanctions.
